title: Pilot integration: latency burn-in + routing experiments
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on latency burn-in results, egress shaping experiments, kernel compatibility after upgrade, and routing fallback behavior. Team reviewed benchmark CSV and decided rollback plan for the 2.3 kernel on one nodepool, plus action items for a 4k concurrent stress test and security docs handoff.
topics: KV cache warmup and hit rates
action_items: Devon Patel: run 4k concurrent requests stress test against canary pool and upload pilot-bench-results.csv (due 2025-06-02)
Lina Park: provide podlevel network egress metrics and current iptables rules snippet (due 2025-05-30)
Avery Chen: share updated rollback playbook + SOC2 snippets to Priya (due 2025-05-29)
next_steps: Schedule deep-dive with kernel eng if 4k test fails
Run quantization experiment on a small model shard next week
Customer to validate KV cache warmup after kernel rollback
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-05-27
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~50 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (CSM), Lina Park (BrightLane), Marc Diaz (BrightLane), Priya Rao (BrightLane), Tom G.

Optional auto sections:
Summary: quick pass over the burn-in numbers and the kernel upgrade impact. we have a small regression on p95 after the 2.3 kernels; nodal differences look network-ey.
Topics: see metadata above.
Action items: listed in metadata; also Devon will attach raw traces and pprof outputs to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.internal/pilot/pilot-bench-results.csv - placeholder).

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: alright everyone, thanks for joining. letting folks trickle in but we can start. main objectives — quick status, numbers from the burn-in, and decide on the rollback or mitigation.
[00:18] Lina Park: yep thanks. appreciate the timing. we ran the overnight ramp to 2k rps, and then stepped to 4k for an hour. uploaded a trimmed csv. there are spikes at the 10 and 30 minute marks.
[00:32] Devon Patel: I pulled the csv earlier, the p50 stayed steady, p95 jumped from 210ms to 420ms on nodepool A right after the kernel flip. nodepool B (still on 2.2) stayed at expected. so it's strongly correlated with the kernel.
[00:46] Marc Diaz: and just to be clear, nodepool A had the new 2.3 kernel with the updated egress shaping rules we pushed?
[00:55] Lina Park: yeah, we applied the egress shaping (tc) and the iptables rule set as part of the rollout. I thought maybe the shaping is throttling bursts and causing queueing?
[01:08] Tom G.: we also saw a KV cache miss rate increase right after the roll — not sure if that's related to small pointer alignment changes in the runtime with the kernel.
[01:18] Devon Patel: possible. we do rely on user-space irq handling for our kernel bypass path; small timing diffs can change how the runtime batches.
[01:29] Avery Chen: ok so two hypotheses: shaping queueing + kernel scheduling differences affecting batching and KV cache warmup. let's triage in parallel.
[01:40] Priya Rao: security note — before any rollback or new kernel pushes we'll need the updated SBOM and attestations. send to me and I'll route to infra audit.
[01:48] Avery Chen: noted, Priya. I'll put the SBOM bits and SOC2 snippets into the security pack.
[01:53] Maya Ortiz: quick ask — are we still confident routing fallback to hosted models is seamless if private capacity degrades? customer said their user facing flows can tolerate some slowdowns but not error spikes.
[02:05] Devon Patel: we tested fallback last week. functionally it works but there is a latency delta — fallback to hosted adds 80–160ms depending on region. that was acceptable in our SLO conversation but needs to be explicit in the playbook.
[02:18] Lina Park: ok that's good to know. we want automatic fallback only for non-critical routes.
[02:24] Avery Chen: will add per-route annotation in the rollout config.

[02:40] [~10m mark - deep dive into numbers]
[02:42] Devon Patel: I put up the p95 graph — the canary's p99 shows a heavier tail at the three minute mark (link). interestingly the KV hit rate dips from 92% to 68% which aligns with the latency tail.
[02:58] Marc Diaz: can you explain why the hit rate would drop after a kernel change? is there eviction behaviour tied to glibc?
[03:08] Devon Patel: not glibc directly — more likely scheduling jitter causing the runtime's async flush to run less predictably; which causes more cold lookups. small but multiplies at high concurrency.
[03:22] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry interjection — did we also change the prefetcher flags in the build?
[03:28] Devon Patel: no prefetch flags changed in this build, so that helps narrow it down.

[03:45] [~18m mark - mitigation brainstorm]
[03:46] Avery Chen: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel on nodepool A, 2) tune tc rules to be more permissive for short bursts, 3) adjust batching window at the runtime to be slightly larger to absorb jitter. tradeoffs?
[03:59] Marc Diaz: rollback is simplest and lowest risk. we can schedule a rolling rollback to half the pool tonight.
[04:06] Priya Rao: from security/compliance angle rollback is fine, but you need to capture the change events — so make sure logging and audit shows the rollback window.
[04:15] Lina Park: if we rollback we need to confirm KV warmup — last time after a change we needed ~15 minutes of steady traffic to hit normal hit rates.
[04:26] Devon Patel: I'll instrument a synthetic warmup sequence post-rollback to speed cache warmup.

[04:40] [~28m mark - stress test plan]
[04:42] Devon Patel: proposed plan: run a controlled 4k concurrent test against a canary subset after rollback. collect p50/p95/p99, KV hit rate, cpu steal, network tx/rx queues. I'll upload the raw pprof traces.
[04:58] Tom G.: is it okay if we run that during daylight? we'll need to coordinate with platform on-call for potential autoscale churn.
[05:05] Marc Diaz: yes coordinate. do not run without backup steps.
[05:09] Avery Chen: backup steps: automatic fallback to hosted route, circuit break on error rate > 2% sustained, and immediate rollback triggers. I'll write those into the rollback doc.

[05:30] [~38m mark - security and docs]
[05:32] Priya Rao: also we need KMS key rotation info and details on request-level encryption in transit between VPC endpoints. we've seen a few vendors forget to include ephemeral keys in playbooks.
[05:44] Avery Chen: good point. we'll include KMS flow diagrams and key rotation schedule.

[05:55] [~45m mark - closeout and next steps]
[05:56] Lina Park: so recap from our side — we'll permit rollback to 2.2 on nodepool A tonight, share egress metrics, and be on-call for the 4k run.
[06:06] Avery Chen: Redwood will share the rollback playbook, attach the SOC2 snippets, and Devon will run the stress test and share results.
[06:13] Marc Diaz: can you also add a short runbook note about how fallback affects per-route cost? finance wants a rough delta.
[06:20] Avery Chen: yes — I'll add cost delta estimates (hosted fallback token cost vs private).

[06:30] Maya Ortiz: thanks everyone, see you next week.

[END]
